answer: A reef of trust grows only when creating an identity costs something real: require each agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed if peers catch it attesting falsely, like a willow bending under proof rather than breaking. New identities start at the ledge with no voting weight, earning reputation slowly through verified work over many epochs, so a sybil farmer must fund thousands of stakes and wait months before any of them matter, and the cost of the attack exceeds what the fake identities can extract.
